description.text:
Companion of treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 for clients that
identify outputs through the wlr-output-management protocol. It lets
a client obtain the same stable treeland_output_uuid_v1 object from
a zwlr_output_head_v1 instead of a wl_output.

A zwlr_output_head_v1 is advertised by the wlr-output-management
protocol even while the output is disabled and has no live wl_output
global, so this protocol lets clients identify an output in that
state. The uuid returned for a head is the same uuid that
treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1.get_uuid returns for the wl_output
of the same physical output device.

The treeland_output_uuid_v1 interface, including the meaning and
stability of the uuid, is defined by
treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 and is not duplicated here; this
protocol only adds a second factory that creates the same object.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.
description.summary: output uuid identity from wlr output heads

description.text:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects
from zwlr_output_head_v1 objects. The client calls get_uuid for
each head it wants to identify; the compositor reports the uuid in
the initial uuid event on the returned object. Multiple uuid
objects may be created for the same output, whether through this
manager or through treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1; each reports
independently.
description.summary: factory for output uuid objects from wlr heads

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_output_uuid_head_manager_v1 object and
release the client's binding to the manager global.

Existing treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects created through
this manager are not affected and must be destroyed
separately by the client.

Create a treeland_output_uuid_v1 object for the output
represented by the given zwlr_output_head_v1. The head may be
in any state, including disabled: a wlr_output_head is
advertised even when the output is turned off, so this request
can identify an output with no live wl_output global.
description.summary: create a uuid object for a wlr output head

args.name: head
args.summary: the wlr output head to identify
